newsitem.title: HONG KONG: More in Hong Kong hopeful of economic future - paper.
newsitem.headline: More in Hong Kong hopeful of economic future - paper.

text.p: Hong Kong people are becoming more optimistic about the territory's economic and political future, the results of a quarterly newspaper survey showed on Monday.

Up to 20 percent of people surveyed expected Hong Kong's economic environment to improve over the next 12 months while the number who thought the situation would deteriorate fell to 25 percent from 36 percent previously, the English-language South China Morning Post (SCMP) said.
The quarterly survey, commissioned by SCMP and the Chinese-language daily Ming Pao, was conducted by Survey Research Hong Kong (SRH) from October 7 to 11.
Some 75 percent were confident or very confident about Hong Kong's political future, up from 70 percent in the last survey.
A political confidence index monitored by SRH also edged up to 91 from 90 in July and 86 in January, the newspaper reported.
The SRH economic index also rose to 87, compared with 83 in July and 73 a year ago, it said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for over a century and a half, reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
